display_name: Read the durable record of gauge alarms that fired
description: GAU-21 (2026-08-19). Reads the durable, attributable record of gauge notices the session sweep actually decided to fire, newest first, filtered by detector type, by subject session, and by an inclusive lower bound on emitted_at. Before this record existed the sweep's gauge alarms were appended only as in-memory bridge events, and four independent properties of that queue each defeated an audit: nothing persisted them, so a restart lost every un-drained one; the only reader REMOVED what it read, so a verifier polling the queue raced the steward and could swallow the very alarm the steward needed; no surface was keyed on event type; and the notify path resolved the steward binding first and returned early when it was absent, so an alarm about an unbound session reached nobody and left nothing behind. The consequence was that a missed alarm and an alarm that never fired were the same silence -- the same shape as the original gauge freeze, one level up, where the instrument's own output was unobservable after the moment. Each record carries the SUBJECT session the alarm is about (never the steward it was addressed to), emitted_at on the sweep's own clock at the moment it decided to fire, the steward it was addressed to (null meaning no steward was resolved -- a real outcome, not a missing value), and delivery_outcome as one of appended, no_steward_binding, or append_failed: deliberately not a boolean, because an unbound steward and a failed append are different faults with different owners and both look identical from outside. release_id names the release whose detector fired it, self-identified from the running module's own tree, because the deployed detector's thresholds have already been measured to differ from the source everyone reads: on 2026-08-19 the running release evaluated gauge coverage at 300s against master's 600s and carried no staleness detector at all. threshold_s and observed_s record the threshold in force and the value measured against it at emit time rather than leaving a reader to re-derive them from constants that may not be the ones that fired. last_report_alive_at and gauge_measured_at carry the two diverging clocks for a staleness alarm and are null for a coverage alarm, which fires precisely because there is no gauge row to read. Reading is non-destructive and bounded, with truncated published rather than implied. Retention is bounded by the writer itself at 64 records per subject per type, hard-deleted at write time -- no reaper, and no soft-delete flag that nothing ever clears.
embedding_description: Checking whether the fleet's gauge alarms actually fired for a session and what happened to them, including alarms that were raised but reached no steward at all, rather than only seeing the alarms that happened to be delivered and read.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: entries (newest first: notice_type, agent_instance_id, emitted_at, steward_instance_id, delivery_outcome, release_id, threshold_s, observed_s, last_report_alive_at, gauge_measured_at), returned, truncated, queried_agent_instance_id, agent_instance_id (the id records are keyed on after the watch-id join), id_resolution, notice_type, since, retention, delivery_outcomes, notice_types.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with what fired and what became of it: group by delivery_outcome before summarising counts, because a run of no_steward_binding records is a different operational story from a run of appended ones -- the alarms fired and nobody was told. Always quote threshold_s beside observed_s rather than describing an alarm as merely 'stale', and name release_id when comparing records, since two records from different releases may have been judged against different thresholds. Treat a null release_id as 'the release could not be determined' and never substitute the current one. A null steward_instance_id means no steward was resolved, not that the field was unrecorded. If truncated is true, say the record continues past this page rather than describing the oldest entry as the first alarm. An empty result means no alarm was recorded for this filter -- report that as no recorded alarm, never as proof the subject was healthy, since a detector that is not deployed records nothing at all.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Records with delivery_outcome no_steward_binding are an escalation in their own right: the detector is working and its output is going nowhere, which no steward can notice by waiting. append_failed points at the bridge rather than the detector. A gauge_stale_notice record is the freeze signature and its gauge_measured_at is the arrested reading itself -- the value the upsert-only cache would otherwise have overwritten, so it is worth quoting verbatim.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One bounded ordered page over gauge_notice_record, optionally preceded by one peer-binding join to resolve the subject id, both through the state interface.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: invalid_argument: notice_type was not one of gauge_stale_notice or gauge_coverage_notice. missing_argument: agent_instance_id was supplied but blank -- omit it entirely to read every subject. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound. ambiguous_agent_session_id: more than one gauge row claims the same stable session id, so the watch-id join cannot say which session was meant. An empty page is NOT an error and returns a normal successful result with returned=0.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For invalid_argument, use one of the values published in notice_types on any successful reply, or omit notice_type to read both. For missing_argument, omit agent_instance_id rather than passing an empty string. For ambiguous_agent_session_id, inspect the named rows rather than retrying: two live sessions sharing one agent_session_id is stale or duplicate data to reconcile. If a filter returns nothing and you expected records, widen the window with since before concluding no alarm fired, and confirm the detector is deployed in the running release -- an undeployed detector writes no records.
